SEC-HD-V6-01.note: Head noun 'The mat' is singular; participial (D) leaves the sentence without a finite verb.

SEC-HD-V6-02.note: Nominative absolute; finite (A)/(D) make a comma splice, and (C) wrongly separates the absolute's subject from its participle.

SEC-HD-V6-04.note: (B) 'reverted' is plural-compatible and only clashes on tense; a simple past report inside a generic frame is a stylistic inconsistency, not a breach of agreement, so the item leans on tense consistency alone to exclude it.

SEC-HD-V6-05.note: Subject is the fronted 'Where'-clause, hence singular; the relative options leave a fragment.

SEC-HD-V6-08.note: (A) has the same required comma before 'but'; coordinating a nominal clause ('how the tide sets') with two noun phrases is a parallelism preference rather than an outright violation, so (A) is defensible in edited English.

SEC-HD-V6-10.note: Relative verb takes plural 'the bees'; the main verb takes singular 'The number'.

SEC-HD-V6-11.note: Dash must be closed with a dash and the verb agrees with plural 'the calls'.

SEC-HD-V6-18.note: 'not because ... but because' with singular 'the price ... was falling'; (C) strands the later finite verb.

SEC-HD-V6-19.note: 'that work' two words after the blank forces the plural 'beekeepers', killing (C) before the punctuation is even considered; only the comma-vs-nothing contrast is left.

SEC-HD-V6-22.note: (A) 'was falling for fifteen years' is attested English: a past progressive with a durative 'for'-adverbial. The past perfect is better with the 1984 anchor, but the licence for (A) is real rather than a pure error.

SEC-HD-V6-23.note: Fused relative takes subject case from its own clause; 'done' immediately after the blank removes the participial pair but leaves the case contrast intact.

SEC-HD-V6-24.note: Head is singular 'The nightly rise'; 'and' sits inside coordinated of-phrases, and the later 'has never been counted' confirms the number.
